title: What is search worth? Sizing an SEO opportunity honestly
course_title: Search Engine Optimization (SEO): Professional Audits and Client Practice

say: What is search worth? Sizing an SEO opportunity honestly.
This is the video for module one of the professional SEO course.
At beginner level, you learn that SEO helps a business show up on Google.
At professional level, a client asks something harder. How much is better search visibility worth to us, and where should we start?

say: Every search visit passes through the same chain. First, Google shows a page in results. That is an impression.

panel.heading: Four numbers connect search to money
items: Impressions: Google shows the page in results
Clicks: some searchers click (CTR = clicks / impressions)
Conversions: some visitors order, book or ask for a quote
Value per conversion: what each one is worth

say: Some searchers click. Clicks divided by impressions is the click-through rate, or CTR. You find these numbers in Search Console, in the Performance report.

panel.heading: Four numbers connect search to money
items: Impressions: Google shows the page in results
Clicks: some searchers click (CTR = clicks / impressions)
Conversions: some visitors order, book or ask for a quote
Value per conversion: what each one is worth

say: Some visitors take a valuable action, like an order, a booking or a quote request. That is a conversion.

panel.heading: Four numbers connect search to money
items: Impressions: Google shows the page in results
Clicks: some searchers click (CTR = clicks / impressions)
Conversions: some visitors order, book or ask for a quote
Value per conversion: what each one is worth

say: Finally, each conversion is worth some amount. The owner tells you the average order or job value.

say: Step one. Remove branded queries, the ones with the business name. People searching those already know the business. Non-branded queries describe a need, and that is where SEO wins new customers.

panel.heading: Sizing the opportunity
items: Filter out branded queries
Keep non-branded queries at position 8 to 20
Use the site's own CTR for positions 3 to 5
Build an optimistic and a conservative case

say: Step two. Find striking-distance queries, at an average position of about 8 to 20. Google already sees the page as relevant, so improving it is usually the faster win.

panel.heading: Sizing the opportunity

Use the site's own CTR for positions 3 to 5

say: Step three. Do not use CTR charts from the internet. Look at the client's own queries in positions 3 to 5 and use their average CTR.

say: Step four. Build two cases. An optimistic one with that CTR, and a conservative one with half of it.

say: Google's own guidance says no one can guarantee a number one ranking. So label your estimate as a scenario, show the inputs and the formula, and give both cases.

panel.rule: Give a range with your working. Never promise a ranking.

say: Kemi's query, ankara fabric wholesale lagos, had 12,000 impressions, 96 clicks and an average position of 11.4 over three months.
Her queries in positions 3 to 5 average a 6% CTR, and 1.5% of her organic visitors place an order.

say: In the optimistic case, 6% gives 720 clicks, so 624 extra clicks and about 9 extra orders. That is about 421,200 naira.
So this one query could be worth a range, not a guarantee, and the page deserves attention first.

say: Developers judge you by how precisely you speak. Every server answers with a three-digit status code. 200 means OK.

panel.heading: Status codes you will meet
items: 200: OK, the page can be indexed
301 or 308: moved permanently
302 or 307: temporary redirect
404: not found, fix internal links to it
5xx: server error, Google cannot read it

say: 301 and 308 are permanent. Google treats the new address as the main one.

panel.heading: Status codes you will meet
items: 200: OK, the page can be indexed
301 or 308: moved permanently
302 or 307: temporary redirect
404: not found, fix internal links to it
5xx: server error, Google cannot read it

say: 302 and 307 are temporary. Google follows them but may keep the old address.

panel.heading: Status codes you will meet
items: 200: OK, the page can be indexed
301 or 308: moved permanently
302 or 307: temporary redirect
404: not found, fix internal links to it
5xx: server error, Google cannot read it

say: 404 means not found. 5xx means a server error. And point every old address straight to the final one in one hop, with no redirect chains.

say: A Disallow line in robots.txt stops Google fetching a page, but the page can still be indexed from links.

panel.heading: Blocking crawling is not blocking indexing
left: URL can still be indexed from links
right: Googlebot must crawl to see it
Keeps the page out of results
Never also block it in robots.txt

say: A noindex tag keeps a page out of results, but Google must crawl the page to see it. So if you want a page out of search, use noindex and let Google crawl it.

say: You can work in three markets. Local businesses need local search, simple sites and fast pages on modest phones, because most visitors pay for data by the bundle.

cards.d: A clinic, school or caterer in one city. Local search, fast mobile pages, plain language.
A Lagos brand selling in Ghana and the UK. Country targeting and hreflang.
A company abroad. Technical audits at scale and clear written reports.

say: Multi-country brands need hreflang, which tells Google which version is for which country. Use valid codes like en-NG and en-GB, never en-UK, and every version must list itself and all the others.

say: Remote international clients need technical audits at scale and clear written reports. Many people start local, then add remote work later.

say: To remember. Search value flows through impressions, CTR, conversions and value per conversion. Focus on non-branded queries.
Striking-distance queries are often the fastest wins. Use the client's own numbers and give a range. And never mix up robots.txt and noindex.

panel.heading: Remember
items: Value flows through impressions, CTR, conversions and value
Non-branded queries are where SEO wins new customers
Positions 8 to 20 are often the fastest wins
Use the client's own numbers and always give a range
robots.txt controls crawling, noindex controls indexing
